title: A Learned Generalized Geodesic Distance Function-Based Approach for Node Feature Augmentation on Graphs

problem.claim: The work concerns generating node features for graph-based node classification using generalized geodesic distances.

contributions.claim: Introduces LGGD, an approach that learns a generalized geodesic distance function through a pipeline using training data, graph topology, and node content features to generate node features.
Reports improved performance in node classification tasks and competitive results with state-of-the-art methods on real-world graph datasets.
Demonstrates learnability of parameters in the generalized geodesic equation on graphs and supports dynamic inclusion of new labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the method improves performance on node classification tasks.
The authors report competitive results with state-of-the-art methods on real-world graph datasets.
The authors describe generalized geodesic distances as robust to noise and outliers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Geodesic distances are presented as useful in several manifold-related application areas.
LGGD learns a generalized geodesic distance function from training data, graph topology, and node content features to generate node features.
The method is described as benefiting from robustness of generalized geodesic distances to noise and outliers.
The authors report classification performance, dataset comparisons, parameter learnability, and dynamic inclusion of new labels.

The abstract does not describe the training objective, generalized geodesic equation, or parameterization.
The abstract does not provide details about dynamic label inclusion or robustness evaluation.
